title: Forecast wind-change groups gave no clear 48-hour band score gain in two NHC basins in 2021-2025
abstract: We tested whether forecast wind-change groups improve 90% wind bands for selected NHC forecasts. Each year used only the past five years. In 2021-2025 at 48 hours, group bands reduced mean interval score by 2.18 kt in 1,049 Atlantic cases and 2.93 kt in 759 East Pacific cases. Whole-storm 95% intervals were -5.28 to +0.82 and -7.78 to +2.38 kt. Thus neither primary test gave a clear gain. Group bands narrowed for forecast wind loss and had worse mean scores in that group in both basins. A mean-shift control also gave no clear gain. Recovered forecast winds matched 306 comparable raw A-deck winds exactly in four audit storms. This is a later-period test of a simple forecast-change method, not a test of full IBUS or an NHC-issued probability band. Revised records, sample exclusions, limited audits, coarse groups and conditional intervals limit inference. Code, hashes, aggregate results and independent score checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Coverage of constructed 90% wind bands by forecast wind-change group at 48 h in 2021-2025. Counts and uncertainty are in the text and tables.

citations.reason: Motivates independent verification of public hazard products.
Prior unconditional wind-band test provides the benchmark question and source snapshot description; forecast-change code and test are new.
Established forecast-change conditioning; we test a simpler group method on later years, not IBUS.
